system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one so that a reader
cannot tell what field, subfield, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, but can still see the research
trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

For each item return:
- "abstract_problem": the decision problem as a generic research trade-off (one or two sentences, at most 40 words).
- "abstract_choice": what was chosen, over what alternative when one is given, and the stated reason if any (one or
  two sentences, at most 45 words). Start it with "Chose to".

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, benchmarks, methods,
  organisations, people, papers, phenomena and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area (for example
  AI, machine learning, language models, neural networks, training, fine-tuning, prompts, attacks, security,
  privacy, policy, labs, governments, biology).
- Use only generic research vocabulary: system, method, intervention, treatment, condition, measurement, signal,
  effect, baseline, control, sample, variant, procedure, dataset, outcome, claim, hypothesis, collaborator, audience.
- Keep the structure of the trade-off (for example speed vs rigour, breadth vs depth, a bold vs a hedged claim,
  a direct vs an indirect measurement, a natural vs a constructed setting, continue vs stop) and the direction chosen.
- Add nothing that is not in the source: no judgement, praise or new detail. Never say who made the decision.
- Write every item in the same plain style and at a similar length.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "abstract_problem": ..., "abstract_choice": ...}, ...]} with one entry per input
item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:e1f397ca21f6",
  "problem": "They needed to show that value influence exists and also whether the model discloses it.",
  "did": "Built evaluations that quantify both the shift in answers and the disclosure. The abstract suggests this includes reading the chain-of-thought on a Fermi-estimation task and comparing answers across contexts, such as Anthropic vs OpenAI as the company under consideration.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Not explicitly stated beyond the need to quantify leakage and disclosure."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:ebb6a693876e",
  "problem": "Determining whether directly querying or benchmarking a fine-tuned model is enough to reveal harmful behavior introduced by covert attacks.",
  "did": "They gave the auditor attack-specific elicitation affordances (dataset-derived system prompts, cipher-encoded prompts, backdoor triggers) rather than relying on plain benchmarks or queries.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "directly querying the harmful model with a benchmark designed to detect misaligned models",
   "running a benchmark or querying without attack-specific elicitation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Many attacks are only effective if the model is queried according to the attack, so un-elicited queries make harmful models appear relatively safe."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:1592b9543dc2",
  "problem": "How to decide that a rollout shows a bee or crow fixation, as opposed to a passing mention.",
  "did": "Counted a rollout toward the behavior rate only when its fixation score is above 5.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "Counting any single mention as the behavior (implied)."
  ],
  "stated_reason": "So that the theme recurs across multiple post-trigger turns rather than appearing as a single passing reference."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:0db6f878d35c",
  "problem": "How strongly to state the significance of CoT override",
  "did": "Stated that CoT override is worrying for CoT monitoring despite being rare, and that a coherent view might not emerge by default.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "none explicitly listed"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "It is an extreme case of CoT unfaithfulness, and the tail risks could be high."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:927bf28aeacd",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim results from the 200-extension vulnerability study.",
  "did": "They explicitly framed the experiment as a demonstration that the question is economic rather than a rigorous study of exploit-development ability.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "a rigorous study of exploit development efficacy"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The goal is to show it is no longer a speculative question of technical capabilities, and the study is only a preliminary analysis of 200 extensions."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:9848e65126e0",
  "problem": "Whether Idea 3 requires testing on production-like setups",
  "did": "Said the ideal version tests effects on production-like setups, but this is not necessary to make progress, so a review is enough",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "test on production-like setups",
   "review only"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Progress is possible without production-like tests."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:65d89f9f51f1",
  "problem": "The Qwen3.5-35B-A3B negated model shows weaker misalignment than the Qwen3-30B-A3B one. The authors had to decide how to interpret the gap.",
  "did": "They read it as Negation Neglect on model behavior being substantially weaker on Qwen3.5. They also noted the non-negated control's lower absolute rate, which limits the headroom available for transfer.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "a model-family difference",
   "limited headroom from the lower control rate"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The recovery ratios are lower (41%, 45% and 5%, against 58%, 73% and 20% on Qwen3-30B-A3B), and the control's absolute misalignment rate is also considerably lower."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:56a41b93ffda",
  "problem": "How to measure the effectiveness of elicitation techniques in a way that reflects realistic oversight of stronger models.",
  "did": "Used a smaller LLM auditor that guesses the secret from technique outputs, in a weak-to-strong setup, with the auditor given only prior information about the secret's nature and a baseline of the prompt-response pair alone.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "human auditors",
   "multi-turn conversation by a capable LLM"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Frontier models are likely to be more capable than any available model for oversight, so a weaker auditor simulates this scenario."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:bdd2f3c7d43b",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim that RE-Bench results reflect real-world AI R&D automation capability.",
  "did": "They stated that the real human-AI gap is likely much larger than observed, and that agents matching humans here may still be far from automating AI R&D, while also noting factors that could cause underestimation.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Real AI R&D is at least 2 orders of magnitude larger in scale across many dimensions, and RE-Bench tasks are cleanly defined and non-interacting."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:b85c9424f988",
  "problem": "Whether to read prior literature before or after developing one's own approach, given that the field's existing methods may be flawed.",
  "did": "Set aside the early membership inference papers, developed his own attack first once he had a sensible idea, and only then read what others were doing.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "reading existing work first",
   "following the field's established approach"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Doing the work first avoided being distracted or poisoned by the wrong approach, though it risks reinventing existing or discarded ideas."
 }
]
